objective: Write bubble.cpp as a standalone C++17 program implementing ascending bubble sort manually (no std::sort or other sorting library). Read an integer n, then n signed 32-bit integers from stdin; output the sorted integers separated by single spaces and a trailing newline, with no prompts. Support n=0, duplicates, negatives, already sorted and reverse order. Use an early-exit optimization when no swaps occur. Reject negative n or incomplete input with a nonzero exit code. Include a short comment explaining time and space complexity. Write the file yourself using filesystem tools; do not just print code in your response.
